done_when: forge migrate calls a story finished only when every Tasks row is done in the old Forge's records (.factory/stages.json and task markers); a story with a pending part is not converted as finished and gets a replan draft under .forge-migrate/replan/ like a malformed one, and the dry run says which parts are pending; a test covers a story with one pending part

findings.body: The global stage list is applied to every story without checking its `issue` field. Legacy task IDs can repeat between stories: `.factory/stages.json:2` identifies its owner, while `.factory/stories/FORGE-NEXT-1/decomposition.json:6` and `.factory/stories/FORGE-UPG-2/decomposition.json:6` both use `CORE`. In a copied-in client with this layout, a pending `CORE` in one story overrides another story's completed task marker, incorrectly sending that finished story to replan. Filter the global record by its owning story before matching task IDs.
findings.title: Scope global stages to their owning story

why: forge migrate marks an active plan finished whenever its approval is on main, even when its old-Forge stages still have parts pending (a copied-in client's active story has T1 pending, yet the dry run says every part was done)
